statements.status_notes: CVE-2021-45261 is a release of an invalid pointer in another_hunk() in src/pch.c, reported against GNU patch 2.7 as GNU patch bug 61685 with a crafted patch file that makes patch free an invalid pointer while it reads a context-diff hunk: https://savannah.gnu.org/bugs/?61685. In the most recent archived copy of the report, from September 2025, it is open and holds only the original submission and a possible fix attached by another user: https://web.archive.org/web/20250916235957/https://savannah.gnu.org/bugs/?61685. No commit in the GNU patch repository up to the 2.8.1 release of October 2026, and no NEWS entry, names the bug or the CVE. In 2.8 and 2.8.1 the branch of another_hunk() that handles a context hunk whose old lines are omitted still moves the end of the hunk past old-line slots that are filled in only later, as it did in 2.7.6. Debian lists every release, trixie 2.8-2+deb13u1 included, as unfixed with urgency unimportant: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2021-45261. OSV records 2.7 as the last affected version without naming a fix: https://osv.dev/vulnerability/CVE-2021-45261. This owner builds GNU patch 2.8 from Debian's source package: the published builds are the rebuilds of Debian 2.8-2 and 2.8-2+deb13u1 on amd64 and arm64, whose /usr/bin/patch reports version 2.8 and whose Debian changelogs do not name this CVE. Pending: whether a crafted patch file can still reach the invalid free in GNU patch 2.8, which needs either the upstream change that fixed it identified or the bug reproduced, or the path shown unreachable, against these builds, and which decides between fixed and affected for every published build.
